question.problem:
Compute $P(X\le 0)$ given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{20}(3{x}^{2}+2x+1),\, & -2\le x\le 2, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
If a continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x),$ then 

$$
P(a\le X\le b)={\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Since $f(x)$ is identical to zero for all $x<-2,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 0) & ={\int }_{-2}^{0}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{0}\frac{1}{20}(3{x}^{2}+2x+1)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{20}{\int }_{-2}^{0}3{x}^{2}+2x+1\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{20}{[{x}^{3}+{x}^{2}+x]}_{-2}^{0} \\  & =\frac{1}{20}([{0}^{3}+{0}^{2}+0]-[(-2)^{3}+(-2)^{2}+(-2)]) \\  & =\frac{1}{20}(0-[-8+4-2]) \\  & =\frac{1}{20}\cdot 6 \\  & =\frac{3}{10}.\end{aligned}
$$
